title: Microzone KV sourcing and shim relocation policy to reduce GPU fragmentation
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and implement a microzone-based KV allocation and proactive shim-relocation controller that minimizes durable fragmentation in GPU resident KV caches while preserving latency SLOs for continuous batching workloads. The feature introduces smaller contiguous allocation regions (microzones), an occupancy heatmap, and a background relocation policy that performs hole-shimming and cold-entry compaction during low-util windows. This is intended to reduce external fragmentation that causes OOMs and excess eviction churn on multi-tenant inference nodes.
goals: Reduce measurable KV pool fragmentation score by >= 40% on tail-heavy workloads
Lower unexpected OOM/eviction incidents on inference nodes by >= 30% in production tests
Maintain 99th percentile latency within existing SLOs during relocation and continuous batching
Provide observability (heatmaps and relocation traces) to diagnose allocation hotspots
acceptance_criteria: Allocator can split/merge microzones without pausing inference worker threads
Shim-relocation controller relocates cold entries into holes with end-to-end cancellation and throughput-aware pacing
End-to-end canary run for runtime-1.20 shows fragmentation metric drop >= 40% and no increase in 99th perc latency > 5%
Dashboards surface occupancy heatmap, relocation rate, wasted contiguous bytes, and relocation CPU/GPU overhead
implementation_notes: Introduce microzone class: fixed-size small contiguous page groups (configurable: default 128KB zones)
Track per-microzone occupancy bitmap to locate holes cheaply; emit occupancy histogram every 30s
Implement lightweight shim: a relocation operation that copies a small range to fill a hole and updates indirection in the KV index atomically
Relocation performed by a dedicated defrag worker on node; throttled by token-bucket tied to current batching backlog
Prefer relocating cold/matching-tenancy entries: combine access recency and batch-tenancy affinity to avoid moving hot keys
Expose allocation hints to continuous-batching scheduler to prefer allocating into the same microzone for temporally adjacent requests
Design allocator to honor pinned keys that must remain immutable (customer pinning for private deployments)
rollout_plan: Alpha: runtime local e2e tests + synthetic fragmenting workload (1 week)
Canary: roll out to 5% of capacity in staging, run production-like traces for 2 weeks
Gradual ramp: 10% -> 30% -> 100% with monitoring gates, each step 72h
Fallback: runtime flag to disable relocation and coalesce state cleanup script to revert microzone metadata
